Layout updatemenu button objects

Source: R/zz-gen-layout.R
go_updatemenu_button.Rd

The object for an element of the buttons list of the layout's updatemenu (go_updatemenu()). go_updatemenu_button() creates one, with exactly its properties; a named list with the same properties works too.

Usage

go_updatemenu_button(
  arg = NULL,
  ...,
  args = NULL,
  args2 = NULL,
  execute = NULL,
  label = NULL,
  method = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  templateitemname = NULL,
  visible = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

Arguments

arg

Optional named list, or graph object of the same type, to initialise properties from. Named arguments take precedence.

...

Not used: properties must be named in full.

args

Sets the arguments values to be passed to the Plotly method set in `method` on click. Vector or list of up to 3 element(s).

args2

Sets a 2nd set of `args`, these arguments values are passed to the Plotly method set in `method` when clicking this button while in the active state. Use this to create toggle buttons. Vector or list of up to 3 element(s).

execute

When true, the API method is executed. When false, all other behaviors are the same and command execution is skipped. This may be useful when hooking into, for example, the `plotly_buttonclicked` method and executing the API command manually without losing the benefit of the updatemenu automatically binding to the state of the plot through the specification of `method` and `args`. Logical.

label

Sets the text label to appear on the button. String.

method

Sets the Plotly method to be called on click. If the `skip` method is used, the API updatemenu will function as normal but will perform no API calls and will not bind automatically to state updates. This may be used to create a component interface and attach to updatemenu events manually via JavaScript. One of "restyle", "relayout", "animate", "update", "skip".

name

When used in a template, named items are created in the output figure in addition to any items the figure already has in this array. You can modify these items in the output figure by making your own item with `templateitemname` matching this `name` alongside your modifications (including `visible: false` or `enabled: false` to hide it). Has no effect outside of a template. String.

templateitemname

Used to refer to a named item in this array in the template. Named items from the template will be created even without a matching item in the input figure, but you can modify one by making an item with `templateitemname` matching its `name`, alongside your modifications (including `visible: false` or `enabled: false` to hide it). If there is no template or no matching item, this item will be hidden unless you explicitly show it with `visible: true`. String.

visible

Determines whether or not this button is visible. Logical.

skip_invalid

If TRUE, silently drop invalid properties instead of raising an error.

Value

A go_layout_updatemenu_button object (a named list).

Details

Nested objects are named lists, or objects of the constructors their arguments name. Every property is checked against the plotly.js schema when the object is created or modified. A property may be a one-sided formula (color = ~col): it is kept, and evaluated in the data (then checked) when its trace is added to a figure with add_<trace>() or add_trace().

Examples

mtcars |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(x = ~wt, y = ~mpg, mode = "markers") |>
  update_layout(
    updatemenus = list(
      go_updatemenu(
        buttons = list(go_updatemenu_button(visible = TRUE))
      )
    )
  )
